title: Regular Ultrametric Skeletons
summary: The ultrametric skeleton theorem extracts from every compact metric probability space a subset of ultrametric distortion $O(1/\varepsilon)$ that carries a measure whose balls are controlled by the $(1-\varepsilon)$-power of the original measure on dilated concentric balls. We prove a two-sided version for arbitrary compact metric spaces: for every ball centered on the skeleton, the skeleton measure also has a lower bound in terms of the original measure on a smaller nonconcentric ball contained in it.
